At a time when democratic institutions across the world are facing challenges, young lawyers and policymakers have a special responsibility to protect the Constitution and uphold democratic values, he opined. “A strong democracy must allow its citizens to question the government. A strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government. It is one where every citizen has the freedom to question the government. Never stop questioning, never compromise on your values and never forget the people,” he said. Shivakumar was addressing graduating students at the 34th convocation ceremony of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) at the Jnana Jyothi Auditorium in Bengaluru. In an order dated October 16, Justice Amit Mahajan held that the Central government’s order of August 17, 2018, directing the probe was passed mechanically and without application of mind. “The cavalier manner in which the material, as noted above, has been cited, for justifying the entrusting of the investigation to the SFIO, in the opinion of this Court, ought to be deprecated,” the Court said. items.summary: Senior Advocate Kamal B Trivedi holds the rare distinction of being only the second Advocate General for the State of Gujarat to serve a continuous tenure spanning two decades. Concurrently, he secured a Master’s degree in Personnel Management & Labour Welfare. He joined the Bar in 1977 while also teaching at the Sir LA Shah Law College, MN Law College and the Institute of Company Secretaries as visiting faculty. Trivedi was designated as a senior advocate in 2001. He served as Additional Advocate General before taking charge as Advocate General on April 25, 2006. Water stains and white deposits were found in bathrooms, kitchens, and bedrooms, while prolonged dampness had caused steel structures and duct sheets to corrode. items.title: Delhi police cannot use preventive laws to silence dissent  | LME 170 | Dhanya Rajendran
items.summary: Imagine you are on your way to a protest. You haven't reached the protest site. You haven't broken any law. In fact, you haven't even joined the gathering. And yet, the police stop you. Maybe at the airport, outside your home, or on your way there. They put you in a vehicle. And hours later, they let you go. That is what happened to people in New Delhi in the crackdown on protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. And it wasn't just protesters. Journalists covering the protests were detained. Lawyers trying to reach people in custody were stopped. Phones and cameras were seized. People were taken away from the protest site, and in some cases, before they even got there. The Delhi Police say they were maintaining law and order. But there is a fundamental question here: How much power does the police have to stop a protest before it even begins? And when does preventive policing become a way of preventing dissent? items.title: Legal education goes beyond criminal and constitutional law: CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU convocation
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday said the purpose of legal education extends beyond learning the principles of criminal or constitutional law. The CJI said that law school is a crucible where ideas collide, where convictions are tested, and where the very essence of dialogue is forged. "The purpose of a legal education extends beyond learning the principles of criminal or constitutional law; it rests in the invigorating experience of encountering those who see the world differently than we do," he said. He was speaking as Chancellor at the 34th convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bangalore. Earlier in the address, he spoke about what the legal profession demands. He said lawyers need the courage to defend what is just and the humility to listen to voices that often go unheard. "This intellectual independence also calls for fairness: hearing before judging, distinguishing a person from a position and disagreeing without denying another person’s dignity," he added. items.title: Lucio AI launches Legal Research Agent in Open Beta, offers 25 Free Searches
items.summary: Lucio AI has launched Lucio Research , a legal research agent released as an open beta through Lucio Labs. The tool searches, screens, reads and cites across hundreds of legal sources for each question. It is free to use for one month, with up to 25 searches per user. The launch addresses a familiar constraint in legal research. Much of the time spent on a research question goes into finding and screening material rather than analysing it and research usually ends when time runs out rather than when every relevant authority has been read. Lucio says the beta is designed to test how far that limit can be pushed. Lucio Research runs in two modes. According to the company, Standard mode runs a focused search of the core authorities and typically reviews 300 to 500 sources per question. In-depth mode explores about three times as many sources and checks for gaps, usually returning an answer in under three minutes. The company says it often reviews 800 to 1,500 sources in this mode and more than 2,000 on some questions. items.title: Another rape, another suo motu cognizance, but what happens after?
items.summary: Recently, the Supreme Court, in a suo motu writ petition In Re: Recent rape incidents in Delhi NCR gave directions on institutional reforms for improving women’s safety in the Delhi-NCR region. The Court’s intervention comes in the aftermath of the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year old minor in Delhi’s Aastha Kunj Park. This is not the first instance the Court has taken suo motu cognizance of a matter concerning women’s safety against sexual violence. In 2024, the Court did the same in the RG Kar case and gave directions for the creation of safer working conditions for medical professionals. While such initiatives from the Court are admirable, a harder question to answer is: what happens after such directions are issued? The Court’s directions, without any corresponding enforcement mechanism, fail to achieve the aim that they are issued with. The suo motu cognizance addresses institutional failure as a common denominator in such instances of crimes against women. Justice D N Ray added that women deserve to be protected so that their right to legal remedy does not become illusory due to the inherent difficulties they face while in litigation. "The only test is to be applied is the convenience of the weaker party. While suppression, misdeclaration etc., on the part of the applicant would always have their due weightage before any court of law, the primary ingredient which would influence the decision of the Court would be whether, by transferring a petition from one jurisdiction to the other, the Court has been able to balance the inherent inequality which the party seeking access to legal remedy is faced with," the Court said. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court also imposed a cost of ₹10,000 on Hussain, who is already serving life imprisonment in the Ankit Sharma murder case. "The act attributed to the convict, and for which he stands convicted, is that of providing his house to the rioters for their use. The Court had convicted Hussain on October 10, while acquitting all other accused in the case .
